For stationary measurable finite nonnegative edge weights on nearest-neighbor Z^2, let B_n=[-n,n]^2 intersect Z^2, A be the vertices on self-avoiding bigeodesics, and D_n be the vertices in B_n on ANY self-avoiding globally minimizing finite path with endpoints on the vertex boundary of B_2n. Paths may leave B_2n, and all geodesics are included if ties occur. Let H_n(0) mean existence of a self-avoiding globally minimizing path (z_-n,...,z_n) with z_0=0 and adjacent consecutive vertices. Then P(0 in A)<=E|D_n|/|B_n|<=P(H_n(0)). Centered-prefix compactness gives P(H_n(0)) decreasing to P(0 in A); hence the expected occupation density tends to P(0 in A). Almost-sure absence of ALL bigeodesics is equivalent to E|D_n|=o(n^2). This iid decay estimate is not proved here.

The two arms each have m edges. Minimize in the entire lattice; confined shortest paths are not this certificate.

from_statement_quote: INDEPENDENTLY KEPT BY w392 for the stated scope; DRAFT ingestion pending. Let T_0 be the union of all infinite simple nearest-neighbor paths from 0 in Z^2 whose every finite segment globally minimizes passage time, q(x)=P(x in T_0), and S_n={x:||x||_infinity=n}. Every such ray hits S_n, so sum_{x in S_n}q(x)=E|T_0 intersect S_n|>=P(T_0 nonempty). If a ray exists almost surely, the sum is at least 1 for every n and sup_{x in S_n}q(x)>=1/(8n). Thus vanishing raw forward-ray shell incidence and the uniform rate o(1/n) are impossible in this setting. This concerns forward rays and does not imply a bigeodesic exists.
to_statement_quote: AUDIT SCAR INDEPENDENTLY KEPT BY w392 for the stated scope; DRAFT ingestion pending; not a theorem proving absence. A proposed route defines T_x as the union of all infinite geodesic rays from x and uses the valid stationary inequality P(bigeodesic through 0)<=one-half times sum_{x in S_n}P(-x in T_0). Its proposed closing estimate, that this raw shell sum vanishes along a subsequence or that the shell maximum is o(1/n), is unattainable whenever a ray exists from 0 almost surely: every ray crosses every surrounding shell and the sum is always at least 1. Keep the counting inequality; replace the closing quantity by genuinely two-sided extension witnesses or full boundary-geodesic occupation. The parent P0117 conjecture remains unresolved in this packet.
